sentences: I measure the fabric twice with a tape measure before marking the cutting line with tailor's chalk.
I cut the pattern pieces out with sharp scissors, following the chalk lines as closely as I can.
I pin the right sides of the fabric together, placing pins perpendicular to the seam line.
I thread the needle by wetting the end of the thread and passing it through the eye.
I set the sewing machine to a straight stitch and check the tension on a scrap of fabric.
I sew a seam by guiding the fabric under the presser foot, keeping the edge aligned with the guide.
I hem the bottom of the skirt by folding the fabric up twice and stitching close to the fold.
I attach a button by sewing through the holes with a double thread, making a shank for thickness.
I install a zipper by basting it in place first, then using a zipper foot to stitch close to the teeth.
I make a dart by folding the fabric and stitching from the wide end to the point, tying off the threads.
I gather the fabric by sewing two parallel rows of long stitches and pulling the bobbin threads.
I press the seam allowances open with a hot iron before sewing the next row of stitching.
I read the pattern instructions to determine which pieces to cut and how to assemble them.
I baste the layers together with long, removable stitches to hold them in place before final sewing.
I backstitch at the beginning and end of a seam to secure the threads and prevent unraveling.
I rip out a seam with a seam ripper when the stitches are uneven or the pieces are misaligned.
I choose a thread color that matches the fabric as closely as possible under natural light.
I wind the bobbin by placing the thread through the guide and pressing the pedal until it is full.
I adjust the stitch length on the machine to 2.5 millimeters for a standard seam.
I clip the threads close to the fabric with small scissors after finishing each seam.
